roadmap_item: F4 — light, sky and atmosphere, ring 1, ROUND 2
state: LANDED AND MEASURED, AND IT DOES NOT CLOSE THE ITEM. The hard fail that capped round 1 at 2/10 — `RI-VIS04` §2's own DETECT, `M6 hue_offset` — is STILL A HARD FAIL after this round: 7.16 deg -> 7.32 deg on the sealed judged crop, against a minimum of 15 and a hard fail below 6. I am reporting that as the headline rather than the eleven things I did measure, because it is what the round was for. What this round actually produced is the reason WHY, measured rather than argued, and a lever class ruled out so that round 3 does not spend itself on it again.
WHAT_I_COULD_NOT_DO_STATED_FIRST: I DID NOT MOVE `hue_offset`, AND I NOW BELIEVE F4 ALONE CANNOT. Eleven measured configurations at the pair01 window — seven page-side candidates, three source arms, one control replicate — and the full spread of `hue_offset` on the sealed judged crop is 5.84 to 7.34 degrees. The bar is 15, the hard fail is 6, and this repo's own vendored modern-fidelity plates read 12.49-143.28 on the same instrument in the same session. NOT ONE CONFIGURATION CLEARED 8. The shipped change is the best of them and it is worth +0.16 deg. I am not going to describe that as progress toward 15.

AND WARMING THE KEY — THE REMEDY MY BRIEF NAMED — MEASURED WORSE, NOT BETTER. `hue_offset` on the sealed crop: control 7.16, `warm 0.70` 5.84, `warm 1.00 + cool 0.60` 5.84. Warming the key LOWERS it, consistently, at every strength I tried. The mechanism is legible once measured: the shadow side of this world is ALREADY the warm one — the daytime `hor` triple was (0.760, 0.790, 0.700), a pale yellow-green, and it is what `hemi.color`, `fill.color`, the fog lerp and the probe's `horizon` all take their hue from — so warming a key that is already (1.00, 0.94, 0.82) moves the LIT quartile TOWARD the shadow quartile and closes the gap the metric measures. The brief's premise is falsified by its own instrument and I am recording that rather than tuning around it.

THE CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT MY BRIEF CITED DOES NOT SAY WHAT IT IS SAID TO SAY, AND THIS MATTERS BECAUSE THE WHOLE REMEDY RESTS ON IT. The brief and the r1 verdict both argue: at night `night-moon` sets `keyWarmth: -0.80` and `hue_offset` passes at 22-33 deg; `noon-marsh` sets `keyWarmth: 0.0` and it fails; therefore set `keyWarmth`. READ THE SOURCE: `sky.js:815` applies `keyWarmth` to `sunCol`, which is written to `this.sun.color` — and at 19:30 `sun.intensity` is 0.0126 (the r1 builder measured this off the live scene and wrote it into the recipe comment). The light that actually carries a night frame is `this.moon`, constructed at `sky.js:644` as `new THREE.DirectionalLight(0x8ca9d8, 0)` — a HARDCODED COOL BLUE that NO recipe field touches, `keyWarmth` included. So the night's 22-33 deg comes from a hardcoded blue key against a region-tinted warm ambient, and `keyWarmth: -0.80` is very nearly a no-op there. `keyWarmth` is not the lever the night proves, and setting it by day was measured and refused above.

I RAISED `env` TO 0.55, MEASURED IT, AND TOOK IT BACK OUT — AND THAT WAS AN S59 TRADE I ALMOST SHIPPED. The reasoning was sound: the probe is the only ambient term that carries the sky's hue and is resolvable, round 1 cut it 1.00 -> 0.35, and S60 clause (a) had a measured 1.625x of headroom. Measured, both arms: sealed-crop lit-subset ratio 3.457 -> 2.163, FULL FRAME 3.270 -> 2.015 at tau1 and 1.9845 at tau8 — BELOW THE 2.0 BAR, an outright fail of the piece's own acceptance. It bought `hue_offset` 7.16 -> 7.25. Nine hundredths of a degree for the acceptance. Refused, reverted, and the arm is kept as `metrics/budget-r2-env055-REFUSED.json` so round 3 does not repay for it.

`envGroundBounce` 0.38 -> 0.22 WENT IN AND CAME OUT FOR A WORSE REASON THAN THAT ONE: it was confounded with the other two changes in the same arm and I never gave it an arm of its own, so I do not know what it did. An unmeasured number is not a kept number, and shipping it would have put a value in the file that no measurement supports.

JOB 3 — `overcast-flat` AND `storm` — IS NOT THIS ROUND'S, AND I AM SAYING SO RATHER THAN LEAVING IT AMBIGUOUS. I captured nothing in overcast or storm. My ruling: it belongs to round 3 and it should be its OWN round, not a rider on a colour round, because an overcast sky IS the light source and the S60/M6 battery has to be re-derived for a keyless recipe before any number about it means anything. What I can say that is new: the sky.js change I shipped is BIT-IDENTICAL AT FULL OVERCAST BY CONSTRUCTION — twelve lines below the edit, `hor.lerp(neutralGrey, overcast)` erases it as overcast rises — so this round cannot have moved those two recipes even accidentally, and round 3 inherits them exactly as round 1 left them.

I DID NOT RE-SHOOT THE BEFORE ARM IN MOTION. The twelve-angle orbit I ran is of the SHIPPED build only, so it characterises what a player sees now and is NOT a before/after. The r1 critic's 54 motion frames are of the r1 build and are not comparable to mine. I also captured NO DRIVEN-WALK sequence at all — the r1 critic did (60 frames, displacement measured per capture against HAZARDS §16) and I did not, so on the 'motion, not only many angles' half of the directive this round is WEAKER THAN THE CRITIC THAT JUDGED THE ROUND BEFORE IT. Twelve angles, two hours, zero moving frames.

EVERY CAPTURE IS SOFTWARE (SwiftShader). No Pod, no hardware confirmation of any window. It is differential by construction — all arms of one window run in one process at one pose (HAZARDS §15) — but the BEFORE and AFTER arms of the source change are two processes against two source states, and I did NOT get a byte-identical null control across them, so see the noise-floor entry below rather than assuming determinism.

MY NOISE FLOOR IS LARGE AND I AM NOT HIDING IT. `base_recheck` — the shipped configuration re-captured from an unmoved camera after every other arm — differs from `base` by mean|d|rgb 1.856 on the sealed crop and 2.503 on the full frame. Arms of 8-26 sit on top of that. So `hemi_off` at 2.177 and `fill_off` at 2.038 are 1.17x and 1.10x their own floor: I read them as UNRESOLVED, not as zero, and every conclusion below that rests on them says 'unresolvable', not 'absent'.

I DID NOT RUN THE 08:00 HOUR-SWEEP I SET OUT TO RUN. The first attempt did one hour in five minutes and was killed by its own timeout with nothing written; I killed it by PID and re-scoped. What replaced it is narrower and is reported as what it is: two hours, not thirteen.
`RI-VIS04` §2 IS STILL ABSENT BY ITS OWN DETECT, BEFORE AND AFTER THIS ROUND, and its 'Blocks score above' value is 5. Nothing here changes that and I am not going to argue that it should.

JOB_1 — THE METRIC THE ROUND EXISTS FOR,.the_wrong_way_numbers_stated_as_plainly_: `C_shadow` on the sealed crop falls 14.146 -> 12.377, a 12.5% LOSS, on the arm I shipped. It remains 2.06x the `exterior_daylight` minimum of 6, and `retention` is flat (0.6901 -> 0.6926, above the 0.60 minimum), so `RI-VIS04` §3-D3 is satisfied — but the chroma in the shadows went DOWN on a change whose entire purpose was to put colour into them, and that is the most uncomfortable number in this file. My reading, offered as a hypothesis and not as a result: the shadow side got bluer and simultaneously less saturated, because the new horizon is closer to neutral in a*b* than the old yellow-green was even though it is further from the key in HUE. I did not design an arm that separates those and I am not going to assert it.
JOB_1 — THE METRIC THE ROUND EXISTS FOR,.MY_RULING_AND_WHAT_WOULD_OVERTURN_IT: F4 CANNOT CLOSE `RI-VIS04` §2 BY ITSELF, AND ROUND 3 SHOULD NOT BE ANOTHER LIGHTING-VALUE ROUND. M6 `hue_offset` is a CHROMA-WEIGHTED CIRCULAR MEAN OF HUE over the lit and shadowed quartiles, and a pixel's hue is albedo TIMES illuminant. When every surface in the frame shares one olive albedo — which is precisely what all five Protocol A judges wrote in their own words, *'every surface returns the same flat matte olive-grey'* — the illuminant's hue is a second-order term in the product, and no redistribution of light between four lights of the same intensity budget can make it first-order. The strongest evidence FOR this reading is the one the r1 verdict already published and read the other way: `hue_offset` PASSES at 22-33 deg at night, where the key is a hardcoded (0.549, 0.663, 0.847) blue — an illuminant hue difference far larger than anything reachable by day — and where the frame is dark enough that albedo saturates less. OVERTURNED BY: any configuration of `key`/`sky`/`fill`/`env`/`keyWarmth`/`envGroundBounce` and the sky colours that measures `hue_offset >= 15` on the sealed pair01 crop without failing S60 clause (a). One such measurement kills this ruling outright, and I would rather be shown wrong cheaply than have round 3 assume I am right.

JOB_2 — THE SHADOWS, AND A PREMISE IN MY.what_I_measured: At the Lilmoth settlement pose (yaw 180, 9 m, pitch -14), landed build, `RI-VIS04` §3-D2's own shadow-map ablation mask as a tau curve: 08:00 cast-shadow area 10.431% at tau8 and 14.136% at tau1; 13:00 13.801% at tau8 and 18.895% at tau1. THE 08:00 FRAME IS AT 76% OF THE 13:00 FRAME'S CAST-SHADOW AREA AND BOTH ARE THREE TO FOUR TIMES §3-D2's 3% FLOOR. There is no hole at 08:00 in the quantity §3 names.
JOB_2 — THE SHADOWS, AND A PREMISE IN MY.so_what_is_the_08_00_defect: It is a statement about the GROUND specifically, not about cast shadow, and the two are not the same measurement. The sun at 08:00 reads back off the live scene at elevation 33.704 deg (`sunDirUnit` [0.7203, 0.5549, 0.4162]) — hand-derived from `sky.js`'s `elev = sin((h-6)/24*2pi)` and `dir = (cos(azim)*0.75, elev, sin(azim)*0.75).normalize()`, and the live readback matches to three decimals. That is not a low sun and it is not a fit failure: the readback also gives `shadowCamera.right` 142.845, `shadowNormalBias` 0.09765 and `shadowBias` -8.6562e-5, and 0.09765 is exactly `texel * 1.4` for `texel = 2*142.845/4096`, so `_fitShadow` is doing what its source says at both hours. WHAT I DID NOT DO is separate ground-plane shadow from building self-shadow inside the mask, which is the measurement that would actually answer the brief's question. Round 3 should ask it that way.

AN_INSTRUMENT_RESULT_WORTH_MORE_THAN_MY_.the_problem: `RI-VIS04` §3-D2 specifies `renderer.shadowMap.enabled = false` with every material marked `needsUpdate` — correctly, because the flag is compiled into the program. On this box under SwiftShader that is a full-scene shader recompile per arm, measured at roughly FIVE MINUTES PER HOUR OF A SWEEP: my first thirteen-hour diagnosis did one hour in five minutes and was killed by its own timeout with nothing written.
AN_INSTRUMENT_RESULT_WORTH_MORE_THAN_MY_.the_substitute: `game/vendor/three/three.core.js` REVISION = '180', and r180 carries `LightShadow.intensity`, which is a UNIFORM: the shader computes `shadowValue = 1 - intensity*(1-shadowValue)`, so 0 means fully lit with no program change.

NOT_ASSUMED_EQUIVALENT_—_MEASURED_BOTH_W.the_test_that_settles_it: The two ABLATION FORMS differ from each other by mean|d|luma 0.3368 and area@tau8 0.00034. The SAME CONFIGURATION re-captured twice in the same process differs by 1.0918 and 0.00095. THE TWO FORMS DIFFER BY LESS THAN A THIRD OF THE CAPTURE'S OWN RUN-TO-RUN NOISE, while the signal they are both measuring is 4.086 and 0.10431 — four times and a hundred times the floor respectively.
NOT_ASSUMED_EQUIVALENT_—_MEASURED_BOTH_W.what_it_does_NOT_prove: They are NOT byte-identical (`frames_identical: false` in `metrics/ablation-equivalence.json`), and I have only checked two hours at one pose on one renderer class. This licenses the cheap form for AREA FRACTIONS at daylight exteriors. It does not license it for anything that turns on individual pixels.

AN_INSTRUMENT_RESULT_WORTH_MORE_THAN_MY_.recommendation: `RI-VIS04` §3-D2 should name the uniform form as a permitted implementation with this equivalence run cited, or the clause is unaffordable to run at any breadth on a software renderer — which is the same shape as the clause it replaced being uncomputable in principle.

THINGS_I_GOT_WRONG_IN_FLIGHT_AND_FIXED.1_I_overloaded_the_box_and_it_cost_wall_: I ran three heavy jobs at once and took the load average to 24.25 on 4 cores; `node tools/contention.mjs` returned WAIT. I killed my own plate analysis BY PID (HAZARDS §10 — never `pkill -f`, the fleet shares this box) and ran one browser at a time afterwards. The plate job had already produced eight rows, which is why the instrument validation survived.
THINGS_I_GOT_WRONG_IN_FLIGHT_AND_FIXED.2_an_inherited_flag_parser_ate_my_output: `f4c-analyse.mjs`'s `flag()` returns every non-`--` argument after its flag to the END of argv, so `--vis03 <files> --out <path>` feeds `<path>` to ffmpeg as a 44th input image. It crashed after doing all 43 files and the wrapper still exited 0 — HAZARDS §18's family, from a third direction. Worked around by ordering `--out` first; NOT fixed in the tool, because `tools/visual/` is claimed directory-wide by W1-30V and this is not my file. FILED HERE so the next reader does not lose six minutes to it.
THINGS_I_GOT_WRONG_IN_FLIGHT_AND_FIXED.3_my_own_added_comment_killed_the_tool_o: A backtick inside a template literal. Caught by `node --check` before it cost a run; `node --check` now runs before every launch.
